note: Adapted from Hill's (1942) species-level description, the original in English. Taxonomic doubt (for the lead to verify): the original placed the species in Mirotermes subgenus Mirotermes s.str. (heading 'Mirotermes (Mirotermes) kraepelini Silvestri', Figs. 300–302), not in the subgenus Paracapritermes, which disagrees with the genus name Paracapritermes kraepelinii used in the checklist; this entry is filed under the checklist's genus name and gid, and the locator keeps the original heading. The synonymy includes 1929 Mirotermes argatus Hill (Victoria); the type locality is Mundaring (WA). The original has three sections, winged adult, queen (body length 17.00 mm, abdominal width 4.00 mm) and soldier, with no worker description; the queen measurements are merged into the alate section. The apparently similar species cited under affinities appear in the OCR as 'M. hrisiformis' and 'M. infrequens', the spelling of the former being undetermined. OCR misreadings: 'Pig.'='Fig.', 'Labmm'='Labrum', '10ng 35'='long', 'pro-no turn'='pronotum', 'platycephalus' remains platycephalus, and 'obeuntis' is the specific epithet of a Hamitermes species.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is medium-sized and hairy, the wings dark smoky, the postclypeus about half as long as wide (0.22 × 0.44), the antennae 15-segmented, the pronotum narrower than the head, the radius very short, the media running through the anterior third of the wing, simple or branched, and the cubitus with 8—13 branches. The soldier has the head long and narrow with parallel sides and variable in size, the frontal tubercles large, stout at the base and upturned at the apex, and the antennae 14-segmented. The original states that the species has no close relatives in the southern hemisphere and that the other species of the same genus can be separated from it by size and by the shape of the frontal tubercles alone (the names of the supposedly similar species are defective in the OCR; see the note).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A medium-sized, hairy species, the wings dark smoky. Head, thorax and abdominal tergites dark brown, the postclypeus a lighter brown, the labrum pale orange-yellow. Postclypeus length about half its width (0.22 × 0.44). Fontanelle variable, usually lanceolate, sometimes prolonged forwards or indistinctly forked. Compound eyes rather large and protruding. Ocelli variable in size, the inner margin slightly raised. Apical tooth of the mandibles not much larger than tooth 2. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 very small; segment 4 larger than segment 3; segment 5 smaller than segment 4 but larger than segment 3. Pronotum narrower than the head, the anterior margin concave, the anterolateral angles rounded, the sides rounded into the wide, wavy posterior margin. Posterior margin of mesonotum and metanotum narrowed and deeply, sharply concave. Radius very short; media running through the anterior third of the wing, simple or branched; cubitus with 8—13 branches. Measurements: body length with wings 11.00 mm; body length without wings 5.25—5.50 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 0.91—1.06 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.65—0.69 mm; head width 0.90—0.95 mm; maximum diameter of compound eye 0.23—0.25 mm; ocellus length 0.06—0.10 mm; pronotum length 0.44—0.47 mm; pronotum width 0.74—0.80 mm; forewing length 9.50 mm; forewing width 2.40—2.50 mm. Queen: body length 17.00 mm; abdominal width 4.00 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head, antennae and palpi pale orange-yellow, the thorax and legs straw-coloured. Head long and narrow with parallel sides, variable in size. Labrum variable, usually with parallel sides and truncate anteriorly, but often with the anterolateral angles prolonged into points. Frontal tubercles large, variable in size, stout at the base and upturned at the apex. Antennae 14-segmented; segments 3 and 4 equal in length and the shortest of all, or segment 4 shorter than segment 3; segment 5 slightly longer than segment 4; segments 6—14 slender, progressively longer. Measurements: body length 4.25—5.80 mm; head length (including mandibles) 2.56—3.08 mm; head length (to apex of frontal tubercles) 1.30—2.00 mm; head width 0.85—1.21 mm; pronotum length 0.25—0.33 mm; pronotum width 0.56—0.73 mm.
